presentation: R[u]/(P,Pu) is a complete intersection of dimension 3; S is a localization of the mult-1 component on the simple-fold open

argument.step1: R = Q[A,B,Y,Z,u] is a UFD and Cohen-Macaulay of dimension 5
argument.step2: content(P)=1 as sealed primitive integer polynomial (1593 terms); verified by producer/verifier gcd of all coefficients
argument.step3: Res_u(P,Pu) is nonzero in Q[A,B,Y,Z] because the sealed irreducible H of degree 43 divides Res_u(P,Pu) and H != 0 (37992 terms, sealed target_branch_global)
argument.step4: Any common divisor of P and Pu in R: if deg_u >= 1 then Res_u(P,Pu)=0, contradiction; if deg_u = 0 then it divides content(P), hence is a unit in Q. Therefore gcd(P,Pu)=1 in R
argument.step5: height(P,Pu)=2 (no height-1 prime contains both). Two generators of height 2 in a CM ring form a regular sequence
argument.step6: R/(P,Pu) is a complete intersection of pure dimension 3, hence Cohen-Macaulay, hence satisfies S_k for all k (in particular S2)
argument.step7: Cohen-Macaulayness is preserved by localization. On the open where complementary resultant factor G and gates Sigma are inverted, H vanishes on V(P,Pu), so S is a localization of (an open of) this CI and is CM, hence S2

betti_note: not computed; CM follows from CI presentation without free resolution
not_claimed: that (P,Pu) is radical globally (only that it is a regular sequence / CI)
